mcq.question: Which comment adds the most value next to `return cups * 236.588;`?

options.B: `// US recipes use the customary cup, not the 250 ml metric cup`

mcq.explanation: Good comments explain why the code is the way it is. Repeating what the expression already says adds nothing and goes stale when the code changes.

mcq.question: Where should a function's Doxygen `@param`, `@return` and `@throws` documentation live in this project?

options.A: In the header, on the declaration that callers read
options.B: In the `.cpp` file, next to the implementation
options.D: In the commit message that added the function

mcq.explanation: Documentation describes the contract callers rely on, so it belongs where callers look: the declaration in the header. Implementation notes explaining why can live in the `.cpp` file.

bonus.question: Some teams require a doc comment on every function; others say good names make most comments unnecessary. Where do you draw the line?
Write a failing test showing that `find_undocumented` reports a function whose doc comment is separated from it by a blank line, then decide whether that is right and make the test agree.
